name: Austin
meta_description: TDSC investigative consulting in matters touching Austin: technology and semiconductor diligence, Texas Business Court support and state agency research.
hero_lede: Austin combines the Texas state capital with one of the most technology-intensive economies in the United States. TDSC scopes investigative consulting from Nashville for matters touching Austin, using public records and coordinating Texas-licensed investigators and counsel where local work is required.
intro: Austin is the Texas state capital and the centre of the Austin-Round Rock-San Marcos metropolitan area, which covers Bastrop, Caldwell, Hays, Travis and Williamson counties and had about 2.56 million residents on 1 January 2025, according to HUD. Government, education and technology anchor the economy. The State of Texas and the University of Texas at Austin are the largest employers, followed by Tesla with about 20,000 local workers. Samsung, Dell and AMD run significant operations, and the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas reports that IT manufacturing and services is nearly three times as concentrated in the metro as nationally. Austin startups attracted 4.1 billion dollars of venture funding in the first half of 2025.

Organisations commission investigative work connected to Austin because fast growth, venture capital and public money meet there. Investors back young technology companies whose founders, intellectual property and revenue claims have short track records. Semiconductor and advanced manufacturing projects, including Samsung's Taylor fab supported by federal CHIPS Act funding, draw contractors, suppliers and joint venture partners whose backgrounds need checking. As the seat of state government, Austin also hosts the agencies, regulators and procurement decisions that companies across Texas deal with. And since September 2024 the Texas Business Court has had a division in Austin, adding a forum for corporate and commercial disputes where factual research can matter.

matters.title: Technology startup and founder diligence
matters.text: Austin's venture market funds young companies with limited histories. Before investment or acquisition we review founders' prior ventures, litigation, regulatory history and intellectual property ownership across Texas, Delaware and other states, testing claims made in pitch materials against public records and identifying undisclosed disputes or related parties.

matters.title: Semiconductor supply chain counterparties
matters.text: Chip fabrication and advanced manufacturing projects around Austin and Taylor involve many contractors, suppliers and foreign affiliates. We research ownership, sanctions and export control exposure, litigation and performance history of counterparties so clients can assess integrity and reliability before awarding contracts or entering joint ventures.

matters.title: Texas Business Court litigation support
matters.text: Governance, securities, intellectual property and large contract disputes may be heard in the Business Court's Third Division in Austin. We support counsel with corporate history, witness backgrounds and document trail reconstruction, scoped to the court's rules and the discovery available in the matter.

matters.title: State contracting and lobbying research
matters.text: Austin is where Texas agencies award contracts and grants and where lobbyists and trade groups engage the Legislature. We review public procurement records, campaign finance and lobby filings, and corporate links between bidders, intermediaries and officials to support integrity reviews, bid protests and internal inquiries.

matters.title: Trade secret and employee departures
matters.text: Engineers and executives move frequently between Austin technology employers. Where a client suspects confidential information left with a departing employee, we research new business ventures, entity formations, patent filings and public statements so counsel can assess trade secret claims, within the limits of lawful public sources.

local_context.title: Texas Business Court in Austin
local_context.text: The Texas Business Court began operating in September 2024 with five divisions, including the Third Division in Austin, and its centralized clerk's office is also in Austin. HB 40, effective 1 September 2025, lowered the amount-in-controversy threshold for most categories from 10 million to 5 million dollars, allowed related transactions to be combined, and added intellectual property, trade secret and certain arbitration matters. Appeals go to the Fifteenth Court of Appeals, a statewide court that also hears cases involving the State of Texas and its agencies.

local_context.title: State and federal courts
local_context.text: Travis County district courts hear general civil and commercial litigation, and because Austin is the state capital many suits against state agencies and officials are filed there. Federal fraud, securities, patent and commercial cases are heard in the Western District of Texas, which has an Austin Division. Counsel selects the forum, and we tailor research to its procedural rules and the records it makes available.

local_context.title: Texas investigator licensing
local_context.text: Texas regulates private investigators and investigations companies under Chapter 1702 of the Occupations Code, administered by the Private Security Program of the Texas Department of Public Safety, which is headquartered in Austin. Licensing involves fingerprint-based background checks, and unlicensed activity is pursued. Attorneys engaged in the practice of law are excluded. TDSC does not hold a Texas licence and coordinates Texas-licensed professionals for any fieldwork in the Austin area.

local_context.title: State agencies and registries
local_context.text: Texas entities are formed with the Texas Secretary of State in Austin, whose records show registered agents and some governing persons, while public information reports filed with the Comptroller often list officers and directors. Austin is also home to the state's principal agencies and licensing boards. Real property records for Austin are kept by the Travis, Williamson and Hays county clerks, depending on location, and appraisal data is published by each county's appraisal district.

tdsc_approach: TDSC has no office in Austin and works on Austin matters from Nashville. We agree the purpose with the client's counsel first, whether a technology investment, a semiconductor or manufacturing counterparty, a Texas Business Court or federal dispute, a state procurement question or a trade secret concern, and scope the research to it. Sources include Texas Secretary of State and Comptroller filings, Delaware and other state entity records, county court and property records, federal dockets in the Western District of Texas, patent, procurement, lobby and campaign finance records, and media. Any fieldwork in Texas is carried out by investigators licensed through the Department of Public Safety. Reports identify sources and confidence levels so counsel can rely on them.

faqs.q: Does an investigator need a Texas licence to work in Austin?
faqs.a: Generally yes. Chapter 1702 of the Texas Occupations Code requires private investigators and investigations companies to be licensed through the Private Security Program of the Texas Department of Public Safety. Attorneys practising law are excluded. TDSC does not hold a Texas licence and coordinates Texas-licensed professionals for any local work in Austin or elsewhere in the state.

faqs.q: What changed at the Texas Business Court in 2025?
faqs.a: HB 40, effective 1 September 2025, lowered the amount-in-controversy threshold for most case categories from 10 million to 5 million dollars, allowed related transactions to be aggregated, and extended jurisdiction to intellectual property, trade secret and certain arbitration-related matters. The Third Division sits in Austin. Counsel decides whether a case qualifies; we scope research to the forum.

faqs.q: How do you check an Austin technology startup before investing?
faqs.a: We identify founders, officers and affiliated entities through Texas, Delaware and other state records and securities filings, then review litigation, bankruptcies, regulatory actions, patent ownership and media. We compare what we find with representations in pitch and diligence materials. The aim is to confirm who controls the company and whether material problems were disclosed.

faqs.q: Can you vet suppliers to semiconductor projects near Austin?
faqs.a: Yes. We research a supplier's ownership and affiliates, including foreign parents, along with litigation, regulatory and sanctions exposure, and its performance record on comparable projects. Screening against US export control and sanctions lists is part of the work. Research is limited to lawful public and commercial sources and is scoped to the decision the client faces.

faqs.q: Can you research dealings with Texas state agencies?
faqs.a: We review publicly available procurement awards, contract records, lobby registrations, campaign finance disclosures and corporate filings to show relationships between bidders, intermediaries and decision-makers. We do not access restricted government systems. This work supports counsel in bid protests, compliance reviews and internal investigations involving Texas public contracts.
